title: Making Friends in Spanish: Phrases to Connect for Real
seo_title: Making Friends in Spanish: Phrases to Connect for Real
meta_description: Making friends in Spanish: introducing yourself, finding common interests, making plans, keeping in touch and deepening friendships, with cultural tips.
excerpt: From ¿De dónde eres? to ¿Quedamos el sábado?: how friendships start in Spanish.

body_html:
Making friends in Spanish is the best reason to learn the language, and the best way to improve it. But the step from polite small talk to real friendship can feel big when you’re working in a second language. The good news: Spanish-speaking cultures are generally warm and social, and people are often delighted that you’re speaking their language. This guide takes you through every stage, from the first introduction to making plans and keeping in touch.

Key takeaways
  • Start simple: ¿De dónde eres?, ¿A qué te dedicas?
  • Find common ground: ¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?
  • Make a concrete plan: ¿Nos vemos el sábado? (in Spain, ¿Quedamos el sábado?)
  • Follow up: a quick message after meeting goes a long way.
{{toc}}

Making friends in Spanish: the first conversation

SpanishEnglish
Hola, soy Tom. ¿Y tú?Hi, I’m Tom. And you?
¿De dónde eres?Where are you from?
¿A qué te dedicas?What do you do?
¿Cuánto tiempo llevas aquí?How long have you been here?
¿Cómo conoces a Ana?How do you know Ana?
¡Encantado/a de conocerte!Nice to meet you!

For more openers and conversation fillers, see {{link:small-talk-in-spanish|small talk in Spanish}}.

Finding things in common

  • ¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre? What do you do in your free time?
  • ¿Te gusta el fútbol / la música / leer? Do you like soccer / music / reading?
  • ¡Yo también! ¿Qué tipo de música escuchas? Me too! What kind of music do you listen to?
  • ¿Has visto la última película de…? Have you seen the latest movie by…?
  • Tenemos que ir juntos algún día. We should go together some day.

Remember a mí también after me gusta; see {{link:tambien-vs-tampoco|también vs tampoco}}.

{{image:2}}

Making plans

  • ¿Nos vemos para tomar algo? Shall we meet for a drink? (in Spain, ¿Quedamos?)
  • ¿Quieres ir al cine el viernes? Do you want to go to the movies on Friday?
  • ¿Qué haces este finde? What are you doing this weekend?
  • ¿Me pasas tu número? Can you give me your number?
  • Te agrego por Instagram. I’ll add you on Instagram.
  • ¿Te viene bien el sábado? Does Saturday suit you?

In Spain you’ll hear quedar for making plans; see {{link:quedar-vs-quedarse|quedar vs quedarse}}.

Keeping in touch

  • Me lo pasé genial ayer. ¡Repetimos pronto! I had a great time yesterday. Let’s do it again soon!
  • ¿Qué tal todo? Hace mucho que no hablamos. How’s everything? We haven’t talked in ages.
  • Me acordé de ti al ver esto. I thought of you when I saw this.
  • A ver si nos vemos pronto. Let’s try to meet up soon.
{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

Where to meet people

If you live in or visit a Spanish-speaking country, the easiest places to make friends are shared activities: language exchanges (intercambios de idiomas), sports clubs, dance classes, hiking groups, volunteering and courses. Outside Spanish-speaking countries, look for local Latin American or Spanish cultural associations, conversation groups and online communities. The key is repetition: seeing the same people every week turns acquaintances (conocidos) into friends (amigos). The Centro Virtual Cervantes also lists Instituto Cervantes centers worldwide, many of which run cultural events where learners and native speakers mix.

Deepening a friendship

Real friendship in Spanish often moves fast and feels warm: people may invite you to family meals, birthdays or weekends away quite soon. Accept when you can, and return the gesture. Phrases that build closeness include Puedes contar conmigo (You can count on me), Gracias por estar ahí (Thanks for being there) and Eres un gran amigo (You’re a great friend). Sharing feelings openly is normal; see {{link:talking-about-feelings-in-spanish|talking about feelings in Spanish}}.

A sample conversation

  • A: Oye, ¿tú también vienes a clase de salsa los martes? (Hey, do you also come to salsa class on Tuesdays?)
  • B: Sí, aunque bailo fatal, jaja. (Yes, although I’m a terrible dancer, haha.)
  • A: ¡Yo igual! Algunos vamos a tomar algo después. ¿Te vienes? (Me too! Some of us are going for a drink afterward. Want to come?)
  • B: ¡Me encantaría! ¿Me pasas tu número para el grupo? (I’d love to! Can you give me your number for the group?)

Cultural notes

Many Spanish speakers socialize in groups rather than one-to-one, so being added to a WhatsApp group is a big step toward friendship. Plans can be flexible: a las ocho may mean eight-thirty, and evenings start later than in the US. Don’t be surprised by physical warmth: kisses on the cheek, hugs and touching an arm while talking are normal. And when someone says Mi casa es tu casa, they usually mean it.

One more tip: when someone invites you and you can’t go, suggest another time straight away, Este sábado no puedo, pero ¿qué tal el domingo?, so the invitation doesn’t fade.

And if you’re nervous about your Spanish, say so with a smile: Estoy aprendiendo, ¡ten paciencia conmigo! Most people will love helping you.

Common mistakes

MistakeBetterWhy
¿Qué haces? (meaning your job)¿A qué te dedicas?¿Qué haces? = what are you doing now?
Me gustas mucho (to a new friend)Me caes muy bien.Me gustas is romantic
¿Quieres colgar fuera?¿Nos vemos? / ¿Salimos?“Hang out” doesn’t translate
Somos conocidos (for close friends)Somos amigos.Conocido = acquaintance

Final thoughts

Ask questions, find common ground, make a real plan and follow up. Friendship in Spanish happens one ¿Nos vemos? at a time. For more everyday situations, see {{link:spanish-phrases-for-everyday-situations|my guide to Spanish phrases for everyday situations}}.

faq.q: How do you make friends in Spanish?
faq.a: Start with simple questions (¿De dónde eres?, ¿A qué te dedicas?), find shared interests, make a concrete plan (¿Nos vemos el sábado?) and follow up with a message.

faq.q: How do you say “hang out” in Spanish?
faq.a: Vernos or salir: ¿Nos vemos en la tarde?, ¿Salimos el viernes? In Spain, quedar: ¿Quedamos esta tarde?

faq.q: How do you say “I like you” to a friend in Spanish?
faq.a: Me caes muy bien. Avoid me gustas, which sounds romantic.
